newsitem.title: PERU: Peru MRTA rebels leave jungle for Lima - report.
newsitem.headline: Peru MRTA rebels leave jungle for Lima - report.

text.p: Peru's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) is moving its remaining fighters from their jungle headquarters toward the capital Lima to carry out selective attacks, the daily Expreso reported on Sunday.

"The movements of the terrorist criminals from the Tupac Amaru terrorist organisation continue toward the city of Lima ... to carry out terrorist actions in the capital in an escalating and simultaneous manner," Expreso quoted an army intelligence document as saying.

The pro-government newspaper added that a warning had been sent to all diplomatic missions in Lima to beef up security in case an attack was being planned similar to the MRTA's spectacular Dec. 17 takeover of the Japanese ambassador's home, which led to a four-month hostage siege.
Peruvian troops on April 22 killed all 14 MRTA rebels holding the home, in a battle that also left dead two soldiers and one of the group's 72 hostages.
The Dutch Embassy cancelled a party last week as a result of security fears, Expreso said, adding that U.S. companies and institutions could also be targeted by the MRTA.
The newspaper said that as well as attacks in the capital, the Marxist MRTA planned to reactivate propaganda work in the provinces and create unrest in jails.

Analysts estimate that the MRTA has barely 200 active fighters in its ranks. With most of its leaders dead or in jail, the MRTA's new commander is a Peruvian recently returned from Europe named Hugo Avellaneda, security force sources say.
